title: unify-gpu-dep-staging-and-runtime-slimdown
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket consolidates the staging artifacts and runtime dependency paths for CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS into a single deterministic packaging and compatibility layer. The goal is to remove duplicate symbol resolution paths, shrink per-node runtime footprints, and make kernel selection deterministic across heterogeneous fleets while preserving hot fallback paths for quantized kernels.

Background:
Over time our runtime has accumulated multiple side-by-side loaders and heuristics for GEMM/attention kernels: legacy RT shims, a CUTLASS shim, and a Triton plugin probe. These were added incrementally to support different GPU generations and experiment branches. The result is increased probe latency, ambiguous symbol resolution during upgrades, and larger container images. Several customer incidents were traced to inconsistent kernel selection under mixed-version fleets.

Objectives:
- Introduce a single staging bundle format (.rdbundle) that contains signed kernel candidates and a small runtime manifest for deterministic selection.
- Refactor the probe path to use a single probe shim that records decisions to trace/logging and consults a compatibility-policy table rather than hard-coded heuristics.
- Remove at least two legacy loaders from the runtime image and reduce uncompressed GPU runtime footprint by >=18%.
- Provide a compatibility migration mode (runtime-1.22.compat) that allows rolling upgrade with telemetry and safe rollback.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting CUTLASS kernels or changing performance heuristics beyond mechanical selection and packaging.

Risks:
- Incorrect symbol isolation could break existing pinned workloads (P0 customers) if rollout isn't staged.
- Signed bundle verification must not add significant start latency.

Stakeholders:
- Serving runtime (owner), Infra release, QA perf, Security (for bundle signing), Solutions Eng for customer rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic kernel selection produces identical kernel selection decisions across identically configured nodes (same manifest) in 100 test runs.
Runtime image size reduced by at least 18% uncompressed in the default runtime profile.
Probe latency (cold-start) reduced by >= 30% measured across a set of representative GPU instance types.
Signed .rdbundle is verified on startup and failure modes are observable in Console traces and logs.
A canary rollout plan exists and can be executed to upgrade 1%->10%->100% with automatic rollback on SLA or regression signals.
technical_notes: Introduce rdbundle v1: schema is small JSON manifest + gzipped tarball of .so artifacts + signature (ed25519).
Probe shim becomes single entrypoint: /opt/redwood/bin/kernel_probe -> consults /etc/rdbundle/manifest and compatibility table stored in /var/lib/redwood/compat.
Compatibility table: mapping of model-arch (sm, compute capability) to preferred kernel candidate IDs, with fallback order explicit in manifest.
Signing flow: CI builds kernel candidates, packs rdbundle, CI signs artifact using KMS-backed key; runtime fetches signed bundles from artifact registry using mutual TLS.

Fallback behavior: if validation fails or candidate not available, probe will record to telemetry and select next candidate; if none available, runtime falls back to legacy-compat-mode (explicitly gated).
deployment_plan: Phase 0: Feature branch with rdbundle tooling and unit tests (local dev+CI).
Phase 1: Deploy probe shim and compatibility table read-only on staging images (no removal of legacy loaders). Collect 2 weeks of telemetry under varied loads.
Phase 2: Publish signed rdbundle v1 in canary repo and upgrade 1% of host fleet to runtime-1.22.compat with verbose logging.
Phase 3: If signals green, deprecate two legacy loaders from runtime image (image size drop) and promote compat mode to default on canaries.
Phase 4: Controlled ramp to 100% with automated rollback triggers on latency regressions or increased error rates.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing, signature verification, and fallback ordering.
Integration tests that spin up containers across GPU types (A100, H100, T4, V100) and validate kernel selection stability.
Performance bench harness: run GEMM/attention kernels with representative sequence-length distributions and record P99 token latency and throughput.
Chaos tests: simulate corrupted bundle, transient registry failures, and ensure graceful fallback and observability.
Long-running soak in staging for 7 days to catch memory leaks or symbol resolution edge cases.
metrics_to_monitor: fallback.rate (fraction of requests hitting fallback path)
end-to-end P99 token latency for representative workloads

2026-03-02 - Liam O'Connor: Pushed initial rdbundle schema prototype into feature branch. Added unit tests for manifest parsing. Observed 12% image size reduction before pruning legacy loaders.
2026-03-08 - Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed signing proposal; recommended KMS-backed signing and offline key rotation docs. Security review required flag set to true.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Integration tests added for A100/H100; early probe latency improvement of ~28% on cold start. Still need to validate V100/T4 paths. Planning Phase 1 staging deploy next week.
